clues: This state is globally celebrated for the centuries-old artisanal production of indigo-dyed adire textile cloth, centered in Abeokuta.
Every year, colourful horse-riding families and traditional age-grade societies parade before the Awujale at the Ojude Oba festival in Ijebu Ode.
Its capital is built around Olumo Rock, a massive granite fortress outcrop that sheltered its people during nineteenth-century regional conflicts.

clueMedia.alt: Traditional indigo resist-dyed patterned fabric hung to dry
clueMedia.caption: Traditional Adire textile craft in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Photo: Olaniyan Olushola (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Olaniyan Olushola
clueMedia.fallback: Traditional indigo-dyed adire cloth with intricate resist patterns.

clueMedia.alt: Procession of traditional horse riders in ceremonial attire
clueMedia.caption: Ojude Oba festival in Ijebu Ode, Ogun State. Photo: MediaMOF (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: MediaMOF
clueMedia.fallback: Parade of horse riders and traditional age grades at the annual cultural festival.

clueMedia.alt: Massive towering ancient granite rock and staircase
clueMedia.caption: Olumo Rock in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Photo: Adedayo Adesilola (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Adedayo Adesilola
clueMedia.fallback: Massive granite outcrop that served as a historic natural fortress.

rounds.revealFact: Ogun State's capital Abeokuta takes its name ('under the rock') from Olumo Rock, which served as a fortress for the Egba people in the 1830s.
rounds.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; National Commission for Museums and Monuments Nigeria

clues: Human settlement here traces back to iron-smelting blacksmiths who gathered around the iconic summit of Dala Hill over a thousand years ago.
The ancient city was encircled by massive fourteenth-century earthwork walls that spanned fourteen kilometers, accessed through gates such as Kofar Nasarawa.
The centuries-old Kofar Mata dye pits, founded in 1498, remain among Africa’s oldest operating textile dyeing centers.

clueMedia.alt: Elevated ancient settlement hill overlooking a sprawling city
clueMedia.caption: Dala Hill, historic settlement site in Kano State. Photo: Anasskoko (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Anasskoko
clueMedia.fallback: Historic ancient settlement hill overlooking the city.

clueMedia.alt: Historic earthworks and arched city gate structure
clueMedia.caption: Kofar Nasarawa city gate, Kano State. Photo: Suleiman Umar et al. (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Suleiman Umar, Aminu Abdullahi, Abubakar Yusuf
clueMedia.fallback: Portion of the historic earthworks and city gate structure.

clueMedia.alt: Workers at circular indigo dye pits
clueMedia.caption: Kofar Mata dye pits, Kano State. Photo: Andy Musa Chantu (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Andy Musa Chantu
clueMedia.fallback: Ancient indigo dyeing pits operating for centuries.

rounds.revealFact: Kano was the terminus of ancient trans-Saharan trade routes. The Kofar Mata dye pits were established in 1498 during the reign of Sarki Muhammadu Rumfa.
rounds.source: Kano Chronicle; UNESCO Tentative List (Ancient Kano City Walls)

clues: This state is home to Kainji Dam, commissioned in 1968 across the River Niger, forming one of the country's most vital hydroelectric power stations.
Scenic Gurara Waterfalls spans approximately 300 meters across the Gurara River, tumbling over rocky tiers surrounded by savanna forest.
Guarding the state along the strategic eastern highway corridor stands Zuma Rock, an immense 725-meter inselberg with natural facial contours.

clueMedia.alt: Large concrete hydroelectric dam and spillway across a river
clueMedia.caption: Kainji Dam, Niger State. Photo: Arcgwandu (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Arcgwandu
clueMedia.fallback: Major hydroelectric power station and dam across the Niger River.

clueMedia.alt: Wide tiered waterfalls tumbling over rock ledges
clueMedia.caption: Gurara Waterfalls, Niger State. Photo: Amoghale (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Amoghale
clueMedia.fallback: Scenic cascades tumbling over wide rock tiers surrounded by lush vegetation.

clueMedia.alt: Enormous natural monolith rising prominently above surrounding plains
clueMedia.caption: Zuma Rock, Niger State. Photo: Andy Waite (CC BY-SA 1.0)
clueMedia.author: Andy Waite
clueMedia.fallback: Huge natural monolith rising prominently above the surrounding plains.

rounds.revealFact: Niger State is Nigeria's largest state by land area (spanning over 76,000 km²) and hosts three major hydroelectric dams: Kainji, Jebba, and Shiroro.
rounds.source: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria; Federal Ministry of Power

clues: Groundbreaking archaeological excavations here uncovered 9th-century bronze castings of exquisite artistry and lost-wax mastery at Igbo-Ukwu.
Nestled in a lush rainforest valley, the Ogbunike Caves network has provided sanctuary and spiritual significance for generations.
The historic River Niger Bridge at Onitsha serves as the legendary gateway linking western Nigeria to the commercial heartland of the southeast.

clueMedia.alt: Intricate ancient cast bronze roped vessel artifact
clueMedia.caption: Igbo-Ukwu bronze casting, Anambra State. Photo: Ukabia, Modestusonyeke (CC BY-SA 3.0)
clueMedia.author: Ukabia, Modestusonyeke
clueMedia.fallback: Ancient 9th-century bronze casting with intricate concentric and beaded decoration.

clueMedia.alt: Natural forested valley with rocky cave entrances and springs
clueMedia.caption: Ogbunike Caves, Anambra State. Photo: Favour1215 (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Favour1215
clueMedia.fallback: Network of sandstone caves and freshwater streams nestled in a valley.

clueMedia.alt: Long steel truss bridge spanning across a wide river
clueMedia.caption: River Niger Bridge into Onitsha, Anambra State. Photo: Shiraz Chakera (CC BY-SA 2.0)
clueMedia.author: Shiraz Chakera
clueMedia.fallback: Steel truss bridge spanning the River Niger toward the commercial hub of Onitsha.

rounds.revealFact: The Igbo-Ukwu bronzes date to the 9th century AD, centuries before European contact, demonstrating indigenous West African metallurgical mastery.
rounds.source: Thurstan Shaw (Igbo-Ukwu: An Account of Archaeological Discoveries); UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List

clues: Near the Cameroon border, Agbokim Waterfalls plunges across seven distinct cascading torrents over lush rainforest bluffs.
The high-altitude plateau of Obudu Mountain Resort rises over 1,500 meters above sea level, offering temperate highland climates and rolling green valleys.
Every December, the state capital comes alive with the Calabar Carnival, hailed as Africa's largest street party with dazzling pageantry.

clueMedia.alt: Multiple streams of waterfall plunging over rainforest cliff into a pool
clueMedia.caption: Agbokim Waterfalls, Cross River State. Photo: Ei'eke (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Ei'eke
clueMedia.fallback: Seven-stream waterfall tumbling over steep rainforest cliffs into a calm pool.

clueMedia.caption: Obudu mountain plateau, Cross River State. Photo: Bassnificient (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Bassnificient
clueMedia.fallback: Rolling green mountain peaks and valleys on the high plateau.

clueMedia.alt: Carnival parade participants in vibrant feathered costumes and headdresses
clueMedia.caption: Calabar Carnival dancers, Cross River State. Photo: Raji kunle (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Raji kunle
clueMedia.fallback: Vibrant masquerade and street dancers in colourful feathered regalia.

rounds.revealFact: Cross River National Park is one of the oldest rainforests in Africa, home to endangered Cross River gorillas and rare biodiversity.
rounds.source: Cross River State Tourism Bureau; Nigeria National Parks Service

clues: Visitors walk high above coastal wetlands and secondary forest along the 401-meter suspended canopy walkway at Lekki Conservation Centre.
The distinctive military-peaked-cap shaped National Arts Theatre in Iganmu was commissioned for the landmark FESTAC '77 pan-African festival.
During solemn civic occasions, white-robed Adamu Orisha masquerades holding opambata staffs parade through the historic streets of Isale Eko in the Eyo Festival.

clueMedia.caption: Canopy walkway at Lekki Conservation Centre, Lagos State. Photo: Ashinze (CC BY-SA 4.0)
clueMedia.author: Ashinze
clueMedia.fallback: Suspended wooden canopy walkway stretching high above the coastal reserve.

clueMedia.alt: Prominent military peaked-cap shaped civic arts complex
clueMedia.caption: National Arts Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos State. Photo: Maersk Line (CC BY-SA 2.0)
clueMedia.author: Maersk Line
clueMedia.fallback: Distinctive military-hat shaped national cultural monument.

clueMedia.author: Slashme
clueMedia.fallback: White-robed masquerades holding traditional opambata staffs during the festival.

rounds.revealFact: Lekki Conservation Centre features the longest canopy walkway in Africa (401 meters), built by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation in 1990.
rounds.source: Nigerian Conservation Foundation; Lagos State Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture
